content:
We have a list of many templates. Need to find the one that corresponds to Friedel-Crafts acylation of aryl halide to ketone. Look through the list for a template where reactant includes "Cl-[CH2...]" and product is a carbonyl attached to aromatic. The first entry (reaction_id 96922) has retro_smarts_template: '[c:2]-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[n;H0;D3;+0:7]1:[#7;a:3]:[#7;a:4]:[c:5]:[c:6]:1>>Cl-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[c:2].[#7;a:3]1:[#7;a:4]:[c:5]:[c:6]:[nH;D2;+0:7]:1' This seems to be a substitution of Cl-CH2-aryl with something else, not exactly Friedel-Crafts.

Second entry (reaction_id 82460) similar with Br.

Third entry (reaction_id 992058) retro_smarts_template: '[#7;a:8]-[C:7]-[c:6]1:[c:5]:[c:4]:[c:3](-[CH2;D2;+0:2]-[Cl;H0;D1;+0:1]):[c:10]:[c:9]:1>>Cl-C-[Cl;H0;D1;+0:1].O-[CH2;D2;+0:2]-[c:3]1:[c:4]:[c:5]:[c:6](-[C:7]-[#7;a:8]):[c:9]:[c:10]:1' This seems to involve Cl-C-Cl and O-CH2-aryl etc. Not.

We need a template where forward reaction is aryl halide + acyl chloride -> aryl ketone + HCl. The retro template (retrosynthetic) would be product (aryl ketone) -> aryl halide + acyl chloride. So the retro_smarts_template should have product side (left side) as aryl ketone, and right side as aryl halide + acyl chloride.

Search among list for a template where retro_smarts_template includes something like '[c:...]-C(=O)-...' on left and 'Cl-[c:...]' on right plus maybe 'C(=O)Cl' as other fragment.

Look at entry 1037422: retro_smarts_template: '[#7:7]-[C;H0;D3;+0:6](=[O;D1;H0:8])-[c;H0;D3;+0:1]1:[#7;a:2]:[#7;a:3]:[#7;a:4]:[c:5]:1>>C-O-C(=O)-[c;H0;D3;+0:1]1:[#7;a:2]:[#7;a:3]:[#7;a:4]:[c:5]:1.Cl-c1:c:c:c:c(-Cl):c:1-n1:n:c(-C-O-c2:c:c:c:c:c:2):c(-[C;H0;D3;+0:6](-[#7:7])=[O;D1;H0:8]):n:1'

This seems to involve a phenyl with two Cl substituents and a carbonyl attached to heterocycle. Not exactly.

Entry 1153324: retro_smarts_template: '[#7;a:1]:[#7;a:2]:[n;H0;D3;+0:5](:[c:6])-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[c:2]>>Br-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[c:2].[#7;a:1]:[#7;a:2]:[nH;D2;+0:5]:[c:6]' Not.

Entry 586417: retro_smarts_template: '[O;D1;H0:2]=[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[c:3])-[NH;D2;+0:4]-[c:5]>>Cl-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])-[c:3].F-C(-F)(-F)-C(=O)-[NH;D2;+0:4]-[c:5]' This is amide formation with acyl chloride? Not.

Entry 1838006: retro_smarts_template: '[O;D1;H0:4]=[C;H0;D3;+0:3](-[c:5])-[NH;D2;+0:1]-[c:2]>>C-C-C(=O)-[NH;D2;+0:1]-[c:2].Cl-[C;H0;D3;+0:3](=[O;D1;H0:4])-[c:5]' This looks promising: product side is carbonyl attached to aromatic (O=C...-NH-aryl). The right side includes Cl-aryl and acyl chloride (Cl-C(=O)-aryl). Actually the right side: Cl-[C;H0;D3;+0:3](=[O;D1;H0:4])-[c:5] is an acyl chloride attached to aromatic? Wait Cl-C(=O)-c5 (aryl). That's an acyl chloride attached to aromatic (aryl acyl chloride). The other fragment C-C-C(=O)-[NH;...]-[c:2] is maybe a side chain? Not exactly.

But Friedel-Crafts acylation does not involve amide. So maybe not.

Look at entry 647476: retro_smarts_template: '[O;D1;H0:6]=[C;H0;D3;+0:5](-[c:7])-[NH;D2;+0:4]-[c:3]:[cH;D2;+0:1]:[c:2]>>Cl-[c;H0;D3;+0:1](:[c:2]):[c:3]-[NH2;D1;+0:4].O-[C;H0;D3;+0:5](=[O;D1;H0:6])-[c:7]' This is amide again.

Maybe the template we need is not in this list? Could be earlier entry 96922: retro_smarts_template: '[c:2]-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[n;H0;D3;+0:7]1:[#7;a:3]:[#7;a:4]:[c:5]:[c:6]:1>>Cl-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[c:2].[#7;a:3]1:[#7;a:4]:[c:5]:[c:6]:[nH;D2;+0:7]:1' This is substitution of CH2-aryl with Cl-CH2-aryl. Not.

Maybe the Friedel-Crafts acylation template is not present in this subset because we limited to 20 results. Could increase limit to 100 to get more. Let's try search with functional_groups_broken ['halide'] and functional_groups_formed ['acyl chloride']? But earlier gave empty. Maybe need to search with functional_groups_formed ['acyl chloride'] and broken ['aryl halide']? Already did.

Let's try search with functional_groups_broken ['halide'] and functional_groups_formed ['acyl chloride'] and limit 50.

<thought>We need to locate a retrosynthetic template that corresponds to a Friedel‑Crafts acylation: the forward reaction replaces an aryl halide (Cl) with an acyl group, forming a ketone on the aromatic ring and breaking the C–Cl bond. The template’s mapped reaction SMILES (mapped_rxn) is required, along with its template_id (the integer ID used for searching). The database search tools require at least one list‑type criterion, so we will query the template catalog with a broad criterion that includes the broken functional group “halide”. This will return a set of candidate templates; we can then identify the one that matches a Friedel‑Crafts acylation by inspecting its SMARTS and mapped reaction. Once the correct template is found, we will return its mapped_rxn and template_id.
